description: This bar chart, titled “Researcher Location,” illustrates the number of datasets associated with researchers from different countries or regions over the years 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the year, with labels for each year from 2012 to 2022. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with tick marks at powers of ten. The chart employs a grouped bar format for each year, with six colored bars representing the researcher locations: blue for “Other,” red for “UK,” orange for “USA,” purple for “IT,” green for “IN,” and brown for “DE.” For each year, the bars are arranged side-by-side, with their heights corresponding to the number of datasets contributed by that location. The chart shows that the “Other” category consistently has the highest number of datasets, with values reaching 100 in 2021 and 2022, and 100 in 2020. The “USA” category also shows high values, peaking at 100 in 2021. The “UK” category shows a moderate number of datasets, with values around 10 in 2017 and 2021. The “IT” category has values around 10 in 2017 and 2019, and 10 in 2021. The “IN” category has values around 10 in 2016 and 2021. The “DE” category has values around 10 in 2016 and 2021. The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
